intended_object: A UInt64 hash of the sequence of cell sizes of an ordered partition. It is used internally by the canonical-labelling (individualisation/refinement) algorithm to prune its search, as the docstring and module say.
explanation: The definition starts at position 0 and walks the partition's cells using the `cen` array. At each cell it folds the cell size `cen[i]! - i` into a 64-bit hash with `mixN`, starting from the library's `hashSeed`. This is an implementation detail of a graph canonisation algorithm: an ad hoc hash with a seed and mixing function chosen by the library. It has no counterpart in the mathematical literature. Its only stated property, isomorphism invariance, holds because it depends only on the sequence of cell sizes. That is a fact about the algorithm, not a mathematical object to compare against a standard definition.
